title: People’s Mañanera September 17
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Infrastructure to Connect Mexico  
** Work is underway on 802 km of highways, 4,554 km of rural roads, with 50
billion pesos (US$2.91 billion) being invested for maintenance. In relation to
past highway bailouts, President Claudia Sheinbaum explained that today, with
privately funded projects, “they bear the risk, not the people of Mexico.”

**Mexico Demands Shared Responsibility in the Fight Against Drugs  
** In response to accusations from Washington, Sheinbaum called for reviewing
issues such as drug use, distribution, money laundering, and arms trafficking
in the United States as well. “I would like to hear or see a report on what
the U.S. government is doing and the results there,” she said.

**Sovereignty: Cooperation, Yes; Intervention, No  
** Sheinbaum rejected an alleged, unsourced poll in which Mexicans allegedly
favor U.S. intervention and cited a survey in which nearly 90% of respondents
disagreed. The President reiterated that “any pretext for interference or
intervention must be rejected, because it violates sovereignty and
independence.”

**Mexican Handicrafts: Identity and Pride  
** The President highlighted the value of wearing, using, and recognizing
Mexican handicrafts, as well as the revival of the National Fund for the
Promotion of Arts and Crafts (Fonart). “There is nothing more beautiful than
this; it is our identity, and we must take pride in it,” she declared.

**Memory to Defend Our Identity  
** In explaining her speeches on September 15, the night before Independence
Day, Sheinbaum emphasized that today we name and recognize heroines in
contrast to past attempts to downplay such historical figures. “If you don’t
recognize your heroes or your heroines, you have no memory. And a people
without memory is a people without a compass,” she said.
